### 2026-10-09: Entry #1: I did a ton of research into what the rules for the AIAA Build competition entails and what the PCB could possibly need. I decided on a very small budget STM32 since the task didn't seem to

**9.5h**

Entry #1: I did a ton of research into what the rules for the AIAA Build competition entails and what the PCB could possibly need. I decided on a very small budget STM32 since the task didn't seem to need more computing power, and since I've always wanted to work on a STM32.
I started routing the PCB and drafted the schematic. I'll pick out parts next time. I also went through and cleared up any errors with the electric rules checker.

### 2026-11-16: So after some deliberation with my team, we decided to switch to a 1S battery for no good reason. Good thing I have this specific stm32 microcontroller since it can run well all the way down to 3V, th

**7h**

So after some deliberation with my team, we decided to switch to a 1S battery for no good reason. Good thing I have this specific stm32 microcontroller since it can run well all the way down to 3V, the lowest a 1S LiPo can go so I don't need to worry about making extra space for a boost to 3v3 (or lets just say the battery life of this board will be longer from a fully charged battery). I decided to add a constant current driver for the LED while I'm at it, and I luckily was able to fit everything onto the PCB without any size changes so that the people that took over encasing this PCB don't need to make any changes either.

So instead of the buck converter, we have this constant current driver for the LEDs. Had to painstakingly calculate the resistors for this one based on the datasheet based on the voltage and current draw the LEDs had (2v2 and 700mA draw each) and in series becomes 6v6 and 700mA:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/4f234c7351001e690accb591e9aa855fcfdcac9f3dc2662e31de9a414fc5a7b4.png)

Cleared all the warnings AGAIN. Btw, after further discussion, my electric lead told me to do whatever S battery I wanted so I could've just stuck with the 2S battery design in the end and did extra work 😭. Well, I'm not switching back now since I have a constant current driver comparatively I guess...:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/67aedeed5d167e790a19a0a65da243214cc5379265f5abb0732f2a1018ed2347.png)

Here I circled where it went on the PCB design:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/ee09a7a359ab3bd926d0cfb936d9f1e8346013582d9970e42087960c9b27d3b6.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/8d124bfb9ae4a14ebf23640ca6afa599e3ff96dcc5739be7993fb7c8e31756ac.png)
